title: Strictly henselian $\mathbf P^1$ comparison
statement:
In the setup of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup]: let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a strictly henselian local ring with residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $X_0=\mathbf P^1_s=X\times_Ss$ its closed fibre and $i:X_0\to X$ the closed immersion (the base change of $s\to S$). Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on $X_{\Et}$ and $F_0=i^{-1}F$ its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then for every $q\ge0$ the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]

$$
 i^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X_{0,\Et},F_0)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $F$.

(Scope. Stacks 095T proves this for sheaves of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-modules only, and its proof of PBC for $\mathbf P^1$ never needs more. The torsion case is stated here because the unit sk-thm-p1, step (ii), the users [lemma-weil-pbc-p1-exchange-geometric-stalk] (Steps 2-3) and [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line] (Steps 2 and 4), and the Lean declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_projectiveLine_residueField state it; it is carried by the devissage of the last step, which is not Stacks 095T's route. For the use in [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line] only Steps 1-5 are needed: there $F$ is the inverse image of an injective sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, killed by $r$.)

proof.text: *The setting.* $A$ is strictly henselian, so in particular $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)=s$. The projection $X=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)\to S$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], and so is $X_0=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};s)\to s$; hence $X$ and $X_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proper morphisms are of finite type and separated, and the bases are affine) [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The closed fibre $X\times_SS_0$ of [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero] for the henselian pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and the proper $X\to S$ is $X_0$, with $i$ its inclusion.

source.place: proof of Theorem 095T (theorem-proper-base-change), paragraph 2 (S the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring, X = P^1_S, X_0 = P^1_s)

proof.text: *(a) Restricted injectives are acyclic on the closed fibre.* Let $r$ be a prime and $I$ an injective object of the category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-p1-acyclicity] (in the present setup), $H^q(X_{0,\Et},i^{-1}I)=0$ for $q>0$, cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf; i.e. $i^{-1}I$ is $\Gamma(X_0,-)$-acyclic on $\Ab(X_{0,\Et})$. (This is Stacks Lemma 0A5H, which needs only $A$ henselian; [lemma-weil-pbc-p1-injective-acyclic] states the same and is not cited separately.)

source.place: proof of Theorem 095T, paragraph 2 ("see Lemma 0A5H"); Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover)

proof.text: *(b) Degree zero.* For every abelian sheaf $H$ on $X_{\Et}$ the restriction $\operatorname{res}_H:\Gamma(X,H)\to\Gamma(X_0,i^{-1}H)$, $a\mapsto\eta_{i,H}(a)$ ($\eta_i$ the unit of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$, [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]), is bijective, by [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero] applied to the henselian pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and the proper morphism $X\to S$ (Step 1). As $\eta_i$ is a natural transformation, $\operatorname{res}_H$ is natural in $H$; so for a complex $H^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves the maps $\operatorname{res}_{H^m}$ form an isomorphism of complexes $\Gamma(X,H^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_0,i^{-1}H^\bullet)$.

source.place: proof of Theorem 095T, paragraph 2 ("by Lemma 0A3S"); Lemma 0A3S (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-local), the special case of Lemma 0A0C (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair) for A henselian local

proof.text: *(c) Both sides computed by one complex, for sheaves killed by a prime.* Let $r$ be a prime and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ with $rG=0$. Then $G$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules (the action of $\mathbf Z$ on each $G(U)$ factors through $\mathbf F_r$, and morphisms of abelian sheaves between such sheaves are $\mathbf F_r$-linear). The category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]; embedding $G$ and then the successive cokernels into injectives gives a resolution $\epsilon:G\to I^\bullet$ ($I^m=0$ for $m<0$) by injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves. Kernels and cokernels of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules are those of the underlying abelian sheaves, so $\epsilon$ is also a resolution in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. On $X$: each $I^m$ is $\Gamma(X,-)$-acyclic as an abelian sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic], so by the acyclicity criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity](2) for $v=\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, for any resolution $s:G\to K^\bullet$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves and any morphism of complexes $\iota:I^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ with $\iota\epsilon=s$, $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,\iota))$ is an isomorphism; $K^\bullet$ is K-injective [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,K^\bullet))=H^q(X_{\Et},G)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. On $X_0$: $i^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so $i^{-1}\epsilon:i^{-1}G\to i^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a resolution, by $\Gamma(X_0,-)$-acyclic abelian sheaves (Step 2); by [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity](2) for $v=\Gamma(X_0,-)$, for any resolution $J^\bullet$ of $i^{-1}G$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves and any morphism $\gamma:i^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ over $\mathrm{id}_{i^{-1}G}$, $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X_0,\gamma))$ is an isomorphism onto $H^q(X_{0,\Et},i^{-1}G)$. Between them, Step 3 gives the isomorphism of complexes $\operatorname{res}:\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_0,i^{-1}I^\bullet)$.

source.place: proof of Theorem 095T, paragraph 2 ("choose a resolution F -> I^. by injective sheaves of Z/lZ-modules ... Leray's acyclicity lemma ... This complex computes the left hand side"); Lemma 03FD (sites-cohomology-lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree) for the left hand side

proof.text:
*(d) The map is the pullback $i^*$.* Keep $r,G,\epsilon,I^\bullet$ of Step 4. Choose $s:G\to K^\bullet$ a resolution by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves (a K-injective resolution, [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]); since $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism between bounded below complexes and $K^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, there is a morphism of complexes $\iota:I^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ with $\iota\epsilon=s$ (the comparison underlying [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity](2)). Choose a resolution $\rho:i^{-1}K^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves on $X_{0,\Et}$. By [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], computed with $(K^\bullet,J^\bullet)$ (any choice gives the same map by the independence clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]), $i^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $\Gamma(X,K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}}\Gamma(X_0,i^{-1}K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(\rho)}\Gamma(X_0,J^\bullet)$. Naturality of $\eta_i$ gives $\operatorname{res}\circ\Gamma(X,\iota)=\Gamma(X_0,i^{-1}\iota)\circ\operatorname{res}$ on $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$, hence
$$i^*\circ\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,\iota))=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X_0,\gamma))\circ\mathcal H^q(\operatorname{res}_{I^\bullet}),\qquad\gamma=\rho\circ i^{-1}\iota:i^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet .$$
Here $\gamma\circ i^{-1}\epsilon=\rho\circ i^{-1}s$, so $\gamma$ lies over $\mathrm{id}_{i^{-1}G}$ into the injective resolution $\rho\circ i^{-1}s$ of $i^{-1}G$ (a resolution since $i^{-1}$ is exact). By Step 4 the three maps $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,\iota))$, $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X_0,\gamma))$, $\mathcal H^q(\operatorname{res}_{I^\bullet})$ are isomorphisms; hence $i^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(X_{0,\Et},i^{-1}G)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. (This is the last sentence of clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] with $M^\bullet=i^{-1}I^\bullet$, a complex of $\Gamma(X_0,-)$-acyclic sheaves; clause (2) as stated asks for a map $\beta$ out of the inverse image of the K-injective resolution into $M^\bullet$, which is not at hand here since $\iota$ goes the other way, so the comparison is made directly as above.)

source.place: proof of Theorem 095T, paragraph 2: the identification of the comparison with restriction is left implicit there; written out by the agent

proof.text: *(e) Torsion sheaves.* By Step 5, the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-iso-prime-torsion-devissage] holds for $u=i:X_0\to X$, both schemes being quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Step 1). That lemma gives that $i^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(X_{0,\Et},F_0)$ is bijective for every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge0$. (Stacks 095T has no such step: it works with sheaves of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-modules throughout.)

source.place: devissage of the proof of Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives), paragraphs 2-3, transposed by the agent to global cohomology

proof.text: *Naturality.* For a morphism $\varphi:F\to F'$ of torsion abelian sheaves, $i^*\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(i^{-1}\varphi)\circ i^*$ by the naturality clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial].

proof_origin.place: proof of Theorem 095T (theorem-proper-base-change), paragraph 2, for sheaves killed by a prime (Steps 1-5); the torsion devissage (Step 6) and the identification of the map with the pullback (Step 5) are written by the agent on the pattern of the proof of Lemma 0A4B

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every torsion sheaf $F$ on $X$, restriction induces isomorphisms

$$
H^q(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_0,F_0)\qquad(q\geq0).
$$
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. Exactness of inverse
image along the closed immersion gives an exact complex $F_0\to I_0^\bullet$.
The preceding lemma makes each $I_0^r$ acyclic, so Leray's acyclicity lemma
identifies $R\Gamma(X_0,F_0)$ with $\Gamma(X_0,I_0^\bullet)$. Degree-zero
restriction identifies this complex with $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$ term by term.
Taking cohomology gives the displayed isomorphisms, and naturality follows
from the naturality of the restriction map and of injective resolutions. The
source locators are Tags `0A0C` and `0A3S`.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise (objects of the setup named, the map is the pullback i^* of def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback, scope note). Kept for every torsion F, as the unit sk-thm-p1 step (ii), the two users (lemma-weil-pbc-p1-exchange-geometric-stalk Steps 2-3, prop-weil-pbc-projective-line Steps 2/4) and the Lean declaration state it, rather than narrowing to F_r-modules; the hypothesis gap noted at review (the cited acyclicity covers only injective F_r-sheaves) is closed by a devissage step carried by the new node lem-weil-pbc-pullback-iso-prime-torsion-devissage, which is not Stacks 095T's route (095T stays with Z/l-modules). Proof rewritten from Stacks 095T paragraph 2 in five steps: setting; (a) acyclicity of restricted injective F_r-sheaves (prop-weil-pbc-p1-acyclicity); (b) degree zero (lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero, Stacks 0A3S/0A0C); (c) an injective F_r-resolution computes both sides (enough injectives, abelian acyclicity of injective module sheaves = Stacks 03FD, Leray acyclicity, exactness of i^{-1}); (d) identification with the pullback i^* via a comparison map into an abelian injective resolution (independence clause (1); clause (2) of the functoriality lemma does not apply literally, since the comparison map goes the wrong way); then (e) devissage and naturality. Grab-bags repointed: def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves and def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions dropped from stmt_deps; lemma-weil-pbc-p1-injective-acyclic (duplicate of prop-weil-pbc-p1-acyclicity) dropped from proof_deps; proof_deps = union of uses.
